items.title: West Bengal SIR: Supreme Court to hear plea to allow excluded voters under appeal to vote for upcoming municipal elections
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday said that it will hear the case concerning the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in West Bengal on October 16. Pertinently, the Court on that date will consider whether voters excluded during the SIR process and who have filed appeals against the exclusion, should be allowed to vote for the upcoming municipal elections in the State. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana advanced the hearing amid concerns that voters whose appeals against exclusion from the electoral rolls remain pending may miss the November municipal elections. The Court also discussed prioritising appeals seeking inclusion in the electoral rolls over those seeking deletion of voters. "There are two priorities we are contemplating. One is that appeals filed by persons seeking deletion of voters can be pushed back and taken up at the last stage," said CJI Kant. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The Court was informed that more than one lakh appeals seeking inclusion in the electoral rolls had been decided, with 93% of applicants found eligible for inclusion. Around 1.70 lakh appeals remain pending, counsel told the Court. Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan , appearing in the matter, urged the Court to prioritise appeals concerning voters in municipal areas where elections are due in November. He said that tribunals would need sufficient time to decide these appeals, adding that the elections would have to be notified by November 15. Gopal Sankaranarayanan, Senior Advocate Advocate Prashant Bhushan, also appearing in the matter, highlighted the risk that voters whose appeals remained undecided could be unable to vote in the upcoming elections. “These are deleted voters on whose behalf the petitions have been filed. Their appeals are pending before the tribunals. Municipal elections are due in November. The question is whether they will be able to vote in those elections,” he said. The Court said that it was already considering the issue and would examine whether a solution could be found at the next hearing. items.title: Delhi High Court refuses urgent hearing in Youth Congress petition for permission to protest at Jantar Mantar against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday refused to allow urgent listing of a petition filed by Indian Youth Congress (IYC) challenging the Delhi Police' refusal to permit them to hold a demonstration against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar. The plea filed by IYC national president Uday Bhanu Chib was mentioned before acting Chief Justice Nitin Sambre by Senior Advocate Sanjoy Ghose . Ghose said that he had mentioned the matter yesterday too and the Court had granted him liberty to mention the matter today if it is not listed. "What is the urgency? We will hear it on Monday," Justice Sambre said. Chib has challenged the Delhi Police’s order of October 1 rejecting their application. According to the plea, the IYC had applied on September 25 seeking permission to hold a peaceful demonstration involving around 100-150 people. The organisation said it had undertaken to comply with all lawful conditions relating to security, traffic management, discipline and maintenance of public order. The plea states that despite repeated follow-ups, the police communicated the rejection only on October 1, which was also the first proposed date of the demonstration. According to the petition, the power of the police to regulate assemblies does not extend to imposing a blanket prohibition without an individualised and proportionate assessment of the circumstances. As per the plea, the decision by the police amounts to a violation of fundamental rights to freedom of speech and expression and peaceful assembly under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b) of the Constitution. The plea has challenged the "mechanical application" of guidelines governing protests and assemblies. The plea was filed through advocate Roopesh Singh Bhadauria.

items.title: MKBAC Series: Can non-service of notice invoking Arbitration preclude the impleadment of Non-Signatory Parties in Arbitration?
items.summary: The Indian Supreme Court’s decision in Adavya Projects Pvt. Ltd. v. M/S Vishal Structurals Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. has held that issuing a Notice Invoking Arbitration (NIA) under Section 21 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act (ACA) is mandatory, however non-service of such notice on a person does not preclude their impleadment in the arbitral proceedings. Though prima facie such a proposition might seem dichotomous, a deeper analysis of the judgement exhibits that it is based on sound reasoning which furthers the cause of arbitration, albeit with some potential procedural difficulties which are discussed later in this post. Factual Background The Claimant and the Respondent No.1 (Company) entered into an agreement (the “LLP Agreement”) to form a Limited Liability Partnership (LLP)/(Respondent No. 2) for execution of a project, pursuant to which the Claimant and the Respondent No. 1 entered into a Supplementary Agreement and a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU). Clause 8 of LLP Agreement provided that Respondent No. 3 would be the CEO of the LLP and Clause 40 of the LLP Agreement provided for an arbitration clause. The Respondent No. 3 was also a director in the Respondent No. 1 Company, but only the Claimant and the Respondent No. 1 were signatories to the LLP Agreement. Once disputes arose, the Claimant issued the NIA to the Respondent No. 1 and thereafter the Claimant filed a Section 11 application for appointment of arbitrator, impleading only the Respondent No. 1 as a party. The High Court appointed a sole arbitrator to adjudicate disputes between the parties to the LLP Agreement regarding disputes arising out of the LLP Agreement, the Supplementary Agreement, and the MoU. Non-maintainability of proceedings in the absence of NIA and reference by the High Court Before the arbitrator, the Claimant preferred an application under Section 23(3) of the ACA to amend his statement of claim in order implead the Respondent Nos. 2 & 3 as parties to the arbitration, which was allowed by the Arbitrator. The Respondents filed their Section 16 application challenging the jurisdiction of the arbitrator on the grounds that the arbitration was not maintainable against the Respondent nos. 2 and 3 as they were not parties to the NIA or the application for appointment of arbitrator. items.title: Digital arrest scam: Bombay High Court denies bail to accused whose bank account received ₹4 crore
items.summary: The Aurangabad bench of Bombay High Court recently rejected the anticipatory bail plea of an accused whose bank account was credited with ₹4.03 crore in a ₹7.17 crore digital arrest cyber fraud case [Anuj Saxena v. State & Anr.] Justice RM Joshi held that custodial interrogation of the accused is essential to investigate such cyber crimes and identify the real culprits. Justice RM Joshi (Bombay HC) The case arose from a first information report (FIR) registered in Maharashtra where a doctor was pressured into paying ₹7.17 crore under a digital arrest scam. Investigation revealed that ₹4.03 crore of the defrauded sum was credited directly to the account of the accused, one Anuj Saxena, and subsequently withdrawn. Saxena claimed he ran a charitable institution and shared his bank details to receive a promised ₹20 lakh donation. He further alleged his phone was hacked. However, the Court found no evidence on record to support his hacking defense. Justice Joshi highlighted the severity of digital arrest frauds as he rejected the anticipatory bail prayed by Saxena. “The offence in question is serious in nature. Needless to say that there is increase in the number of persons being defrauded by digital arrests,” the Court observed. The judge warned against accepting unverified explanations from account holders. “Any frivolous or afterthought explanation by the persons whose accounts are credited with crime money would amount to lend encouragement to commission of such crimes,” the bench stated. The court concluded that custodial interrogation in such cases is absolutely necessary in order to investigate into the crime and find perpetrators and real culprits. Advocate PR Dubey appeared for Saxena. Additional public prosecutor RP Gour appeared for State. [Read Order]

items.title: Supreme Court Justice Manoj Misra recuses from hearing case between ISKCON Mumbai and ISKCON Bengaluru
items.summary: Justice Manoj Misra of the Supreme Court recently recused himself from hearing a batch of review petitions filed by International Society of Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON) Mumbai seeking reconsideration of the top court’s May 2025 ruling that recognised ISKCON Bangalore as an independent legal entity and owner of the Hare Krishna Temple in Bengaluru [ ISKCON Mumbai vs. ISKCON Bangalore & Ors. ]. A three-judge bench comprising Justices MM Sundresh , Satish Chandra Sharma , and PK Mishra was earlier hearing the case. The Bench was then reconstituted with Justice Manoj Misra replacing Justice PK Mishra. On October 5, the Court informed that Justice Manoj Misra is recusing from the case citing personal reasons and Justice Sharma is also due to retire in November. Hence, the three-judge bench will have to be reconstituted once again. "The Registry is directed to place the papers of the present matters before Hon’ble the Chief Justice of India for reconstitution of a Bench, as one of us, (Hon’ble Manoj Misra, J.) would like to recuse himself from hearing this matter." the Court noted in its order. Justice PK Mishra, Justice MM Sundresh and Justice SC Sharma The May 16 verdict of the top court had ruled that ISKCON Bangalore is a distinct legal entity registered under the Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960, and not a branch of ISKCON Mumbai. The Court then had upheld the trial court’s finding recognising ISKCON Bangalore’s independent status and ownership of the Hare Krishna Temple in Bengaluru, while setting aside the Karnataka High Court’s 2011 decision that had favoured ISKCON Mumbai. Aggrieved by this decision, ISKCON Mumbai approached the Supreme Court again, seeking review of the May 16 judgement that went against it. A bench of Justices JK Maheshwari and AG Masih on November 8, 2025 delivered a split verdict while considering the review petitions. While Justice Masih dismissed the review petitions, Justice Maheshwari allowed them. This difference in opinion led the matter to be placed before the Chief Justice of India who then constituted the three-judge bench which is slated to be modified for the second time now. During an earlier hearing, the counsel appearing for ISKCON Mumbai had told the Court that there were several judicial admissions that were not taken into consideration by the May 16 judgement. items.title: NYAI launches NYAI AI Studio: India’s first Agentic AI Infrastructure Platform for legal and compliance

Rather than adding yet another point solution to an already crowded legal-technology stack, NYAI AI Studio unites data, agents, models, tools, workflows, institutional knowledge and governance within a single environment, giving every organisation the infrastructure to build an AI practice in its own image. Advocate Dr. Chinmay S. Bhosale , Co-founder, NYAI, shared, “Legal and compliance teams cannot treat AI as merely another productivity application. items.title: Rajah & Tann's Ng Kim Beng on the firm's growth story, AI and PE-backed law firms
items.summary: Ng Kim Beng took over as Managing Partner of Rajah & Tann, Singapore a year back. In this conversation with Bar & Bench's Pallavi Saluja, Kim Beng talks about why the firm has grown from just over 30 lawyers to more than 1,100, why India remains part of the firm's vision and why AI's efficiency gains haven't touched the billable hour just yet. He is candid, too, about what worries him: a wave of US firms turning to private equity funding that Asian firms, without similar backing, may struggle to match. Ng Kim Beng (NKB): My predecessor Patrick Ang laid out: people, processes and practice. On people - making sure we continue to attract and retain the right talent and support their growth. One topic that's very current within the firm is the profession's sustainability and, within that, career prospects for younger lawyers. They're often unfairly labelled as a "softer generation," but I think they come with ambition, drive and motivation, on top of the evergreen qualities of diligence and industry. What's changed is a sense of purpose. In my time, that came easily: you joined a good firm, worked under a good mentor, kept your head down and a path more or less opened up for you. That's changed now. The space is far more crowded, competition among peers is sharper, clients are more sophisticated and technology has accelerated all of it. It's about helping them navigate those conditions and helping them see a future for themselves here. On process, the firm has grown enormously since I joined straight out of university, when we had just over 30 lawyers. Today we're 450 fee earners in Singapore and over 1,100 across Southeast Asia. items.title: Vande Mataram row: 5 Kerala Central Uni students suspended for protesting RSS-linked seminar
items.summary: The Central University of Kerala (CUK), Kasaragod, suspended five student leaders after campus protests against the Vande Mataram national seminar that included a representative from an RSS-afflicted organisation as a keynote speaker. The Chief Proctor suspended the students on October 8, claiming they had disrupted the seminar celebrating the 150th anniversary of the national song Vande Mataram. In addition to the suspensions, the Bekal Police registered a suo motu case against 25 unidentified students under sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for unlawful assembly, rioting, and disobeying a lawful order. The suspension and police action stemmed from an incident that occurred on October 6. A two-day seminar, organised by the Sahitya Akademi in association with the CUK and the ABVP, the student organisation of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), was held to commemorate the 150th anniversary of Vande Mataram. Students opposed the event as the keynote speaker was J Nandakumar, national convener of Prajna Pravah, a Hindutva organisation with close ties to the RSS. The protests and the later police action led to four students being injured. The suspension notice says, “Students are alleged to have engaged in an act purportedly defaming the university in the presence of invited guests, dignitaries, media personnel and staff during the seminar.” The five suspended student activists belong to multiple prominent student organisations, including Syed Ali S and Aaved VB from the Students' Federation of India (SFI), Yaseen from the Kerala Students Union (KSU/NSUI) and Shabeer and Thakkiyuddin from the Muslim Students Federation (MSF). "The University gave the suspension order after 6.00 pm [on October 8] saying it would come into immediate effect. An enquiry committee was formed, but no hearing was conducted. No report has been submitted before issuing a suspension order," Sayed Ali told TNM. Following the suspensions, students began a protest in the University from October 8 evening. University. "We demand the immediate withdrawal of the suspension orders issued against the students and a fair and impartial consideration of the entire incident. If the suspension orders are not withdrawn, students will continue their democratic protest through a sustained boycott of classes until the suspensions are revoked," SFI said in a statement.

items.title: El Niño effect: Andhra declares 388 mandals drought-hit; 283 face severe conditions
items.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government has declared drought in 388 of the state’s 688 mandals across 21 districts for the 2026 kharif season. The government has declared 283 mandals as severely drought-affected and 105 as moderately affected. The Revenue (Disaster Management) Department issued a government order on October 1, following recommendations by the State Drought Committee, which met on September 30 to assess drought conditions. The government opted for an early declaration instead of waiting until the October 31 deadline, citing a significant rainfall deficit and prevailing El Niño conditions. Andhra Pradesh recorded an average rainfall of 197.6 mm between June 1 and August 31, against the normal of 424.3 mm, marking a deficit of 53.4%, according to the government order. The assessment was conducted in accordance with the Government of India's Manual for Drought Management, 2016. The drought declaration covers Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Kakinada, East Godavari, Eluru, Krishna, NTR, Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu, Prakasam, Markapuram, Kurnool, Nandyal, Ananthapuramu, Sri Sathya Sai, YSR Kadapa, Annamayya and Chittoor districts. The assessment involved examining rainfall patterns and dry spells, followed by an evaluation of their impact on agriculture and water availability. The government considered indicators such as sown area, vegetation conditions assessed through remote sensing, soil moisture, reservoir storage and groundwater levels. Ground-level verification was also carried out. The data was sourced from various state departments and agencies, including the Directorate of Economics and Statistics, the Agriculture and Horticulture departments, the Andhra Pradesh Space Applications Centre, the Irrigation Department, the Ground Water Audit Department and Acharya N G Ranga Agricultural University. District collectors have been directed to publish notifications in English and Telugu in their respective district gazettes, specifying the mandals declared drought-affected. Meanwhile, the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) criticised the government for excluding Nellore district from the declaration, claiming that several mandals there had received below-normal rainfall. Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu, meanwhile, said interlinking the Godavari and Cauvery river systems could help southern states tackle drought. items.title: Assam student who reported feeling unsafe on train found dead in Andhra Pradesh
items.summary: A 20-year-old student from Assam, Himashri Boro, was found dead near a railway track in Tekkali in Andhra Pradesh’s Srikakulam district, days after she went missing while travelling aboard the Kanyakumari-Dibrugarh Vivek Express. Her death has raised questions about the circumstances surrounding her disappearance, with her family alleging foul play and demanding a thorough investigation. Himashri, a student of B Borooah College in Guwahati, had travelled to Andhra Pradesh with a dance troupe to participate in cultural programmes. According to her family, she was scheduled to return to Guwahati on October 5 to appear for an examination on October 10. After missing her scheduled train, she boarded the Vivek Express from Visakhapatnam on October 6 to travel home alone. During the journey, Himashri allegedly contacted her friends and family members, saying she felt unsafe in a coach occupied by a group of men. Her family said she also shared a video of the crowded compartment with a friend and spoke about being uncomfortable with the behaviour of some passengers. According to her family, Himashri made a distress call to a friend between 2.30 am and 2.40 am, saying that some men were bullying and misbehaving with her. The friend subsequently contacted the Railway police control room and other helplines, the family alleged. Boro's phone became unreachable soon afterwards. The Railway Protection Force (RPF) and the Government Railway Police (GRP) launched a search after a missing person complaint was filed. Railway police later recovered her luggage from the train's S2 coach. Her belongings, including bags, clothes and documents, were found when the train reached Guwahati, according to her family. Her body was subsequently recovered from a wooded area near the railway tracks in Tekkali, Srikakulam district, on October 7. The railway authorities said a preliminary inquiry suggested that she might have fallen from the moving train. The exact circumstances of her death remain unclear, and the family is awaiting the post-mortem report. Both the GRP in Palasa and the RPF in Srikakulam have registered separate cases in connection with the incident. Himashri's family has alleged negligence on the part of the railway authorities, asking why she could not be traced despite the reported distress calls. Her mother has also expressed suspicion that her daughter may have been murdered and appealed to Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma to ensure a thorough investigation.

items.title: Karnataka: FIR against ex-BJP MLA for using fake death certificates to delete Muslim voters
items.summary: The Vijayapura police in Karnataka have registered separate FIRs against expelled BJP MLA Basanagouda Patil Yatnal and BJP corporator Girish Patil over allegations that they submitted forged documents and false information to get the names of living Muslim voters deleted from electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR). Jalanagar police registered an FIR against Basanagouda Patil Yatnal on October 8 following a complaint by Abdulrazak Moulasab, a 50-year-old vegetable trader from Bagawan Colony in Vijayapura. The complainant alleged that a false death certificate was submitted to the Vijayapura City Corporation along with a letter purportedly issued on the MLA's official letterhead, claiming that he had died. According to the complaint, Abdulrazak is a registered voter in Vijayapura City Assembly constituency. He alleged that the documents were submitted on September 3 to facilitate the deletion of his name from the electoral roll. The FIR has been registered under sections 318(4) (cheating), 336(3) (forgery) and 340(2) (forged document) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. In a separate case, Gandhi Chowk police registered an FIR on October 6 against BJP corporator Girish Patil, a close associate of Basanagouda, following a complaint by Javeed Jakirahmed Indikar, a 32-year-old businessman from Vijayapura. Indikar alleged that Girish Patil submitted Form 7 to the Booth Level Officer (BLO), seeking the deletion of his name from the electoral roll on the grounds that he had permanently moved away from his registered address. He claimed that the application was supported by fabricated documents, despite his being a permanent resident of the area. The FIR invokes sections 318(4) (cheating), 336(4) (forgery), 340(2) (forged document), 192 (intent to cause riot), 196(1) (promoting enmity), 196(2), 353(2) (public mischief) and 61(2) (criminal conspiracy) of the BNS. Police are investigating both cases and examining the documents allegedly submitted to seek the deletion of the voters' names. items.title: A ‘one-man’ Election Commission? Inside the allegations against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
items.summary: On October 6, around 240 Opposition MPs marched towards the Election Commission of India’s office in New Delhi, demanding a meeting with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and seeking his resignation. They were stopped a few hundred metres from the Commission’s office and eventually sat in protest. The Election Commission, however, gave a different account. In a press note issued that evening, it said it learnt through the media that MPs wanted to meet the Commission and that, until 4 pm, no political party representative had sought an appointment. Later, Delhi Police informed the Commission that a delegation led by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi wanted to submit a memorandum. The ECI said the delegation wanted to meet at Parliament House Annexe, whereas its protocol required such meetings to be held at the Commission’s premises. It offered to send a senior-most officer to receive the memorandum, but the MPs declined. The explanation may address the question of procedure. But it does not answer a larger question that has been building around Gyanesh Kumar for more than a year — how does the Chief Election Commissioner deal with political parties that question him and how does he deal with the two Election Commissioners who sit alongside him? The October 6 incident is only the latest in a series of episodes involving the CEC and Opposition parties. Once, Kumar publicly demanded that Rahul Gandhi either substantiate his allegations against the Election Commission through an affidavit or apologise to the nation. In yet another, a political delegation claimed that Kumar asked them to “get lost” within minutes of their meeting. Taken individually, each incident can be explained away as a disagreement between the Commission and a political party. Taken together, they raise questions about the style in which the country’s top election official engages with political stakeholders. ‘Sir, please invite us?’ One of the more striking episodes came on June 9, when a Congress delegation went to the Election Commission over a matter concerning the party’s Rajya Sabha nomination in Madhya Pradesh. Congress leaders were stopped outside the Commission’s office and made to wait. Police cited prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The episode ended with Congress leaders staging a protest at the entrance, while some senior leaders were subsequently allowed inside. items.title: Trump administration targets Infosys, TCS, Wipro; alleges H-1B visa abuse
items.summary: By SEUNG MIN KIM, REBECCA SANTANA and BARBARA ORTUTAY Associated Press President Donald Trump's administration announced Thursday, October 8, it was suspending Microsoft and several other firms from a program allowing foreign workers to apply for green cards, as it also lashed out at universities that bring international students to the U.S. on exchange programs. The announcement by Vice President JD Vance marks the latest swing from the Trump administration at employers and universities that welcome foreign students and workers into the country. Such programs have frequently been targeted by some Trump supporters who argue they undercut American students and workers. Supporters say they allow the U.S. to attract the best talent from around the world and fill important hiring gaps. Supporters of the Republican president have long argued that various programs like H-1B visas — which Vance accused Microsoft of abusing — essentially empower American companies to recruit foreign workers for jobs that end up undercutting Americans. In the wide-ranging announcement, Vance and other top administration officials also called out universities over their use of J-1 visas for international students and information technology outsourcing firms. The announcement came hours before Trump awarded the National Medal of Technology and Innovation to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, part of an event at which he granted some of the nation's most prestigious science and technology awards to his tech billionaire allies. Vance says US workers are replaced with 'foreign indentured servants' Vance said the program from which Microsoft is being suspended requires companies to advertise jobs in America before applying to the Department of Labor to show they need to give a foreign worker a green card because of a lack of American workers. "They'll put an advertisement in a small-town newspaper. They'll go out there and say that 'We have advertised for a position with our company, and nobody is responding to it.' And they will use that lack of response to then go and replace American workers with what is effectively foreign indentured servants," Vance said. "There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has used this system more than Microsoft."
